status: Design concepts for approval; no implementation or hardware validation implied
shared_prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity operating-system interface concept screenshot for the Windows Dev Kit 2023 project. This is an approval mockup, not a running implementation.
Primary request: a beautiful, practical, highly organized modern space-themed OS overlay with custom icons and creative custom controls; expose classic Windows 2000-era system-administration concepts using an entirely original modern visual language.
Style: a polished flat frontal screen capture, wide 16:9 composition, edge-to-edge digital interface, crisp legible typography. Deep space ink-blue backdrop, restrained nebula illumination, luminous silver and muted cyan-violet edges, substantial calm negative space. Sparse stars only behind content. Matte translucent curved surfaces and fine orbital traces, premium and coherent, restrained rather than busy science-fiction HUD. Text is high-contrast, essential controls large enough for practical mouse, keyboard and touch navigation.
Visual system: custom recognizable geometric icons with consistent thin-line weight, softly beveled facets and subtle light, orbital selectors, segmented arc controls, curved focus outlines and spatial work areas. State must be conveyed through readable words as well as color. Keep decorative galaxies out of content text. No conventional rectangular push buttons, no table/list views, no Windows taskbar or start menu, no native dialog controls, no rows of dashboard cards, no gray Windows 2000 styling, no stock Windows/OpenAI/GitHub/Qualcomm logos, no marketing claims.
Text: all interface copy MUST use sentence case: only the initial word of a phrase capitalized, except genuine proper nouns and technical abbreviations such as Windows, GitHub, AI, NPU, CPU, USB, RAM and ARM64. Never use all-caps headings or title case. Use very little text and spell it exactly. Include the small footer "Design concept · Sample data". Do not invent hardware measurements, driver version numbers or claims of an actual successful update.

images.label: Desktop
images.detail:
Screen: desktop overview.
Show a quiet spatial desktop with the exact heading "Your workspace" and small subtitle "Windows Dev Kit 2023".
Four prominent custom orbital portals are arranged in a calm, balanced constellation around a spacious central workspace: "System", "Devices", "Files" and "Maintenance". Each has a unique meaningful icon: a connected-core system symbol, layered microchip for devices, folded luminous file planes, and a repair orbit for maintenance. The central area is mostly open and beautiful. A subtle unobtrusive search constellation near the upper area reads "Find anything". A small status arc reads "Local workspace". A narrow custom curved navigation trace has an obvious selected home node, not a conventional taskbar. Make it a believable useful daily desktop, with the portals clearly being custom controls rather than ornamental planets. One small anchored translucent information surface may read "System overview".

images.label: System hub
images.detail:
Screen: the system-administration hub.
Heading "System"; subtitle "Tools in one place".
Show an elegant spatial map with six clearly separated custom translucent orbital sectors, exact labels "System information", "Services", "Event viewer", "Users and permissions", "Network" and "Storage". Each has a recognizable original icon. Arrange them around a calm central system core, not a grid of cards or a list.
The "Services" sector is in focus and unfolds a flowing curved work surface with three large individually labeled constellation nodes "Running", "Stopped" and "Startup". Use segmented arcs and anchored labels as custom interactive controls. The selected node has a distinct focus contour with a readable word, not only a color difference. Keep the six sectors and selected details legible. Preserve all modern space styling; no retro Windows appearance.

images.label: Drivers and NPU
images.detail:
Screen: device and driver management workspace.
Heading "Devices"; subtitle "Hardware and drivers".
A central abstract physical microchip silhouette for the ARM64 dev kit anchors a clear device constellation with readable exact labels "CPU", "Graphics", "NPU", "Network", "Audio" and "USB". No sprawling decoration or lists.
The "NPU" node is selected. Its attached generous curved glass work surface displays an elegant larger custom NPU icon and exactly "Neural processing unit", "Driver details" and "Compatibility test". Beneath that use a small clearly distinct status caption "Verification pending", with an amber orbital marker. The status is a hypothetical design placeholder, not a real measured fact.
Three custom segmented arc affordances around this detail work surface are labeled "Inspect", "Test" and "Restore". They must appear as thoughtfully designed arc controls with clear focus states, not standard push buttons. Show an obvious route back to "System".

images.label: Files and storage
images.detail:
Screen: a novel practical files-and-storage workspace.
Heading "Files and storage"; subtitle "Space for your work".
Show three distinctive file collections as spacious luminous planes nested in a restrained orbit: exact labels "Projects", "Documents" and "Recovery". A fine curved breadcrumb reads "Workspace / Projects". Individual custom folded-plane file icons are few, large, widely spaced and recognizable, without a conventional explorer sidebar, details view, table, list view or rectangular card grid.
One collection opens as a broad curved transparent shelf revealing three beautiful custom labeled file objects: "Source", "Builds" and "Notes". Integrate the exact label "Find a file" into a small elegant search lens. Include a compact original storage allocation arc with labeled segments "System", "Workspace" and "Recovery", without invented quantities or percentage claims. Use practical hierarchy rather than a random galaxy of unlabeled icons.

images.label: AI maintenance
images.detail:
Screen: the AI-assisted maintenance workspace.
Heading "Maintenance"; subtitle "Review, test and recover".
An understandable calm left-to-right orbital workflow uses five large distinct custom nodes connected by a subtle curved trace: exact labels "Observe", "Review", "Test", "Release" and "Restore". A secondary anchored label reads "GitHub project", another reads "AI helper". Integrate these into the workflow clearly, without logos.
The "Review" node is selected and expands a generous curved translucent surface. It reads exactly "Proposed change", "Review before applying" and "Driver configuration". Show a custom review lens and an amber pending-state halo. A separate small readable guardrail caption "Device changes need approval" is part of the concept UI. No claims that AI can magically modify proprietary Windows internals. Show a visually clear distinction between reviewing a suggestion and installing a release using readable labels, with a restore snapshot orbit visible. No conventional buttons, lists, chat-bubble columns or card grid.

images.label: Custom controls and icons
images.detail:
Screen: a cohesive visual-system approval sheet on the same restrained space backdrop.
Heading "Controls and icons"; subtitle "A consistent visual language".
This is a beautifully organized design sheet, not an OS dashboard. Present three spacious custom-control demonstrations with exact labels "Orbital selector", "Segmented dial" and "Focus contour". Show the selector with three readable choices "System", "Devices", "Files"; show the segmented dial with "Observe", "Review", "Test"; show a keyboard-focus outline on an original curved interactive surface. None may resemble conventional rectangular push buttons.
Below, show eight carefully spaced original thin-line faceted icons, each with a sentence-case label: "System", "Devices", "Network", "Files", "Services", "Events", "Users" and "Recovery". Each icon must be distinct and semantically recognizable, with consistent geometry and stroke weight. A small state study shows the exact labels "Ready", "Pending" and "Attention" using contour shape and words plus color. The sample arrangement is a polished style guide with large breathing room, never a dense list view. Keep typography bright, restrained and readable.
